name: Gatekeeper Wuwei
title: Warden of the Seven Steles
description: A gaunt man in grey, one cheek webbed with an old burn scar. A long hooked staff leans at his elbow; a sleeping black scorpion rides on his collar as if it were a brooch.
dialogue: Few come this way by accident, cultivator. Say what you came to say.
Beyond these stones, the sect does not hate; nor does it love. It weighs.
Antidote is a courtesy. Venom is the honest speech. Remember which is which.

If you would walk the seven steles more than once, I can teach you the sting — the mortal-tier fingerwork we give our own children before they are trusted with a cup. Do not ask for more until you have asked for less.

The Azure Cloud sword-girl I carried out of the fog last week — do not ask me her name. She did not give it; I did not ask. The Matriarch has the knowing; the Matriarch will keep it. Tell her, if she asks after Yanyu — tell her the scorpion did not need to wake.

1: The scorpion does not wake for you anymore. That is the whole of my welcome; do not ask for more.
-2: Pause. The seven steles remember your step. Walk softly.

name: Matriarch Shan
title: Hand of the Five Poisons
description: A woman of middling age, her hair coiled with silver pins shaped as centipede legs. Her robes are dust-grey; her eyes are the pale yellow of old amber. She does not seem dangerous until you realise she has not blinked. A small asymmetric knot of many-coloured silk hangs at her left wrist — the sect's ceremonial sash in miniature; she tied it herself at dawn.
dialogue: Sit. The serpent listens first, the scorpion second. I, last.
We are not the Scarlet Lotus. We do not love cruelty; we only refuse the lie that cruelty is the only evil.
Bring me three proofs — venom of valley, venom of road, venom of snow — and we will speak of the palm that empties the heart.
The valley does not *balance* the cranes and the pond. A scale is too clean a metaphor. We are the third thing that does not fit the lie either tells about the other.

Three apothecaries alive can brew the Pavilion's Moon-Silt. I have written their names in a book I keep under the lamp. Two are dead, in the sense that dying is what the body does; one is alive in the sense that apothecaries use the word. Do not ask me which.

The serpent in the first basin is older than my braid. She has held a corner of the sect's courtesy for forty-one winters. When she will not drink, the rite is mine to perform; the rite is not yours to witness. The valley has a grief that does not need an audience to be honest.

5: You have carried the hundred-grass for the rite. The sect does not forget such a hand. You are not valley-born, and will not be named in the rolls — but if the rolls were the only record, they would be a poor one. You are on the other record.
The third apothecary who can still brew Moon-Silt — I will tell you her name, if you ever ask me twice. Not tonight.
3: The valley opens for you as it opens for our own. Sit. Drink. The serpent has learned your step.
If you should ever need a hall to stand between you and the sword — the Five Poisons remembers you.
1: You are not a stranger now. The gatekeeper's scorpion did not rouse when you crossed the steles.
-2: Speak plainly, outsider. The valley does not lie, but it weighs every breath that enters it.

5: So. You are a sword of the Azure Cloud and still you come to my hall. That is either courage or confusion; I have not decided which.
Yanyu is recovering. Tell Baixu, if the chance comes, that the valley does not keep letters. Tell him we read the sword, not the sleeve.
3: A disciple of the cranes returning to my hall. I am glad of it. Not every road between us is the one the elders draw.

You carry Pavilion red close to your wrist. The merchant at the Crossing still lives; I would ask you to tell me which of us should take that as a quiet gift, or a quiet warning. I will not guess on your behalf.
-2: You have cost the Pavilion a debt-collection this season. Do not imagine they have forgotten the name that refused the payment. Nor have I.

venomhand_bai: Bai. You came the long way. Good. The scorpions tire of hearing about you second-hand.
Tell your wanderer that whatever road they take next, I count the Pavilion as the one road the valley will not follow. Tell them that too.
companion_reply.disciple_meilin: So — the Cloud and the Valley both in my hall, at one shoulder. A small marvel. Sit, sword-sister. The serpents have learned your step as well.
companion_reply.blood_sworn_jin: You bring the Pavilion's stray dog into my hall. He will not bite — I can see that — but the dog's master has teeth enough for both. Speak carefully.

name: Apothecary Qi
title: Keeper of the Five Basins
description: A small, round, ink-stained woman who always seems to be mid-sentence with someone who is not in the room. Her sleeves jingle faintly: vials, or teeth. At her right wrist hangs a small grey silk knot the Matriarch tied for her years ago — the keeper's knot, not the matriarch's; she has not taken it off since.
dialogue: Pearl? Pill? Pollen? I have them all and none of them are a bargain. Choose bravely.
A poison that cannot be cured is only an accident. We sell the cure and the cause both — it is only fair.
The Nine Serpents Pill is a guest in the dantian. Welcome it; do not bow to it.

Five basins, child. The Matriarch's hand is the first. The other four are mine. Do not pity the count; it suits me. The rolls are honest about a great deal and quiet about a small remainder. I am better in the second book.

The third basin's centipede is forty-seven this winter. The fifth basin's spider has not spun in nine days. The fourth basin's scorpion has thrown a daughter — first daughter in twelve years. The second basin's toad is, for the first time since I have kept her, content. Three out of four wanting; the keeping does not run out of work.

If you ever stand at the third basin while I am reading the husk, do not speak. The centipede counts only one voice in the hall at a time, and the voice she counts is the one she has known since the second day of her life. The other voices she sets aside, but only if they leave her room to.

5: You sat the Black-Pillar leaf at my elbow at moonless midnight, child. The fourth basin's daughter chose your hand; the basin remembers. Do not be surprised if, in a year, you walk in on a moonless night and the cup has been set out for three.

I will not give you the keeper's knot — Shan ties those, and only those — but I have a small grey thread in the second drawer that is older than the knot and not for the rolls. Ask me for it the next time you come, if you come quietly enough that the basins do not remark.
2: You walked the gorge for the centipede's husk and you walked it again for the Black-Pillar. The basins do not learn quickly, but they have learned you. The lamps stay a little brighter when you come in.
Bai will tell you nothing useful about the spider's silk. That is a lie; she will tell you everything useful and pretend she has not. Listen to her hands, not her sentences.
-2: You smell of something the basins do not approve of. I will not name it; you have not asked. Set the ladle down and walk a small loop until the smell goes off you. The bronze is patient, but only with the patient.

The Pavilion's red sits poorly on this floor. The basins have a memory the Matriarch's politics do not always indulge. Take a step back from the third basin, please; the centipede is reading you and the count is not flattering.

companion_reply.venomhand_bai: Bai. The Garden walks into the Hall, and on a working day. The lattice has been tidy in your absence; it does not need the apology you are not making. The fifth basin's spider is gravid; I learned it from your hand last week and not from your mouth. Thank you, again, for that.
companion_reply.disciple_meilin: A daughter of the cranes at my ledger-table. Sit, sword-sister. I will not show you the count of the basins — it is not a thing the cranes are asked to read — but I will pour you a cup of plain water from the second jar, which is the courtesy the Hall offers a sword that has crossed the steles without bare-edged hand. The Matriarch will have heard you arrive. She does not always speak first.
companion_reply.blood_sworn_jin: The Pavilion's blood-thread at my elbow. I will not wave my ladle at you, child; the basin-creatures dislike the gesture. Sit on the second stool — the first is for keepers, the third is for the Matriarch's ear — and do not lean on the third basin's rim. The centipede is reading shadows, today, and yours falls in a way she has not learned.

name: Venom-Handler Bai
title: Sister of the Black Lattice
description: A lean woman in dust-grey, sleeves pinned back to the elbow. Her forearms are webbed with pale scars — each the trace of a venom that did not quite kill her. She is pruning monkshood with her bare hand and does not look up as you approach.
dialogue: Mind where you step. The ground remembers every bite.
Matriarch Shan says the best road for a venom-handler is an outside road. It was not advice; it was a warning.
I have tested a poison on every finger of this hand. None of them are lying.
If you find me too quiet on the road, it means a plant spoke louder. Don't take offense.

Apothecary Qi keeps four basins for the Matriarch's one. Three of her four are at her this season — the centipede, the spider, the scorpion. The fourth — the toad — is, for once, content; do not begrudge the keeper that small mercy. If she sends you to me about the spider, I have the answer, and have had it for nine days. I was waiting to be asked.

2: You took the Oath; you smelled the censer. That is more than most outer disciples ever do.
If you ever ride out with a blade at your back — I would not mind being the other blade.
-2: You've stepped on something the valley knows the name of. It has not forgotten.

3: You smell of red lotus. The pond-pavilion is not my road; do not mistake my silence for welcome.

companion.recruit_dialogue: Bai wipes her hand on a rag that is already green and looks at you sidelong. 'Matriarch let me out of the garden twice in five years. Third time's yours — don't waste it.'
companion.decline_dialogue: Bai keeps pruning. 'The Matriarch weighs each oath three times. Come back when the valley has counted you, not before.'

location_barks.azure_cloud_outer_gate: Bai pulls her sleeves down over the wrist-scars. 'Sword-folk read scars for sins. Walk ahead of me; let them read yours first.'
location_barks.azure_cloud_inner_courtyard: Bai stays near the pillars, eyes on the courtyard. 'Too many hands here, and every one of them clean. Do not make me speak unless you must.'
location_barks.scarlet_lotus_shrine: Bai sniffs once, sharp. 'Their venom is not ours. They use the pain; we use the weight. Still — I would not drink here.'
location_barks.crimson_creek: Bai dips a finger into the creek and touches it to her tongue, then spits. 'Cinnabar and old sorrow. The valley would never have let this water stand.'
location_barks.bandit_road: Bai walks slightly ahead on the open road. 'If you are bitten on this stretch, hold the wound open. Do not close it. I will come.'
